confirmed: The source is the 13-page journal article by Avita Salsabila and Siti Maysarah in JIPMat, Volume 10, No. 2, Oktober 2025, pp. 185-197, DOI 10.26877/jipmat.v10i2.2771; submission 2025-09-17, acceptance 2025-10-24 and publication 2025-10-27 are printed on PDF p. 1 (journal p. 185).
The entire markdown and all 13 PDF pages were read, including the reference list ending on journal p. 197. No appendix is included and no supplement is mentioned (PDF pp. 1-13).

There is one original quasi-experiment, with purposive selection of intact classes X-2 (experimental) and X-3 (control); random assignment of people, classes or condition order is not reported. quasi_people, observational context, core = no and criterion 1 = not_met are supported (PDF pp. 5-6, journal pp. 189-190, Metode and Table 1).

The sample counts people: 70 grade-10 students, 35 in each class, from a population of 135 students in four classes in school year 2024/2025. The analysis lists 35 per class and t-test df = 68, supporting 70 analyzed; no separate randomized count or exclusions are reported. The study has at least 50 people overall despite fewer than 50 per arm (PDF p. 1, Abstrak; pp. 5-6, Metode; p. 7, Table 3; p. 9, Table 4).

The intervention lasted 18 days, with three meetings per week in each class; creative thinking used five questions covering fluency, flexibility, originality and elaboration, and adversity quotient used a 32-statement questionnaire (PDF p. 6, journal p. 190, Metode).

Gemini.AI and the SPLDV mathematics material are identified, but the model version and detailed student/teacher interaction with Gemini are not specified (PDF p. 1, title and abstract; pp. 10-11, journal pp. 194-195, discussion and conclusion).

Creative-thinking N-gains are 0,617 experimental versus 0,504 control in the abstract, and 61,65% versus 50,42%, both categorized sedang, in the results (PDF p. 1, journal p. 185, Abstrak; PDF p. 8, journal p. 192, Uji N-Gain).

Every number in the outcome reported string matches Table 4 or the cited prose: equal variances assumed t = -2.1, df = 68, Sig. = .04, mean difference = -.112, SE difference = .054, Levene F = 2.1 and Sig. = .15; not assumed t = -2.1, df = 66.3, Sig. = .04. The accompanying prose gives 0,041 (PDF p. 9, journal p. 193, Table 4 and following paragraph).

Table 2 contains transformed adversity-quotient questionnaire descriptives, not creativity-score descriptives. No creativity arm SDs, standardized effect or confidence interval are printed (PDF p. 7, journal p. 191, Table 2 and preceding paragraph; PDF pp. 8-9, Uji N-Gain and Table 4).

The excluded adversity-quotient questionnaire outcome has N-gain 0,419 versus 0,337 in the abstract and Table 5 reports t = -3.3, df = 68 and Sig. = .001 for equal variances assumed, as stated in the form notes (PDF p. 1, Abstrak; PDF p. 9, journal p. 193, Table 5).

The Shapiro-Wilk inconsistency recorded in notes is real: Table 3 prints creativity-control Sig. .846 and experimental Sig. .062, whereas the prose gives experimental 0,846 and control 0,62 (PDF p. 7, journal p. 191, Table 3; PDF p. 8, journal p. 192, opening paragraph).

This is an original empirical study, not a synthesis; there are no pooled estimates, study counts or standardizers to extract into synthesis (PDF pp. 5-9, journal pp. 189-193, Metode and Hasil dan Pembahasan).
summary: This is one non-random study of 70 students, correctly classified as quasi_people and observational context, and the recorded numbers match the PDF. The after_ai and expert_raters labels are unsupported; incomplete coding fields and the one-line finding's locators also need correction.
